entries.title: Resistor
entries.content: A resistor limits current and divides voltage. Color bands give value: e.g., Brown-Black-Red-Gold = 1kΩ ±5%. Standard series E12: 1, 1.2, 1.5, 1.8, 2.2, 2.7, 3.3, 3.9, 4.7, 5.6, 6.8, 8.2. Power ratings 1/4W, 1/2W, 1W — always use at least 2× dissipation margin.

entries.title: Capacitor
entries.content: A capacitor stores charge between two plates. Q = CV. Blocks DC, passes AC. RC time constant τ = RC — charges to 63% in one τ, ~99% in 5τ. Types: ceramic (small pF-nF), electrolytic (µF, polarized), tantalum. Used for filtering, coupling, timing, decoupling.

entries.title: Inductor
entries.content: An inductor stores energy in a magnetic field when current flows through a coil. V = L(di/dt). It opposes sudden current changes — passes DC, blocks AC. Unit: Henry (H). Used in filters, transformers, SMPS, RF tuned circuits (LC resonance f = 1/(2π√LC)).

entries.title: Diode
entries.content: A diode allows current one way only. Forward voltage: silicon ~0.7V, germanium ~0.3V, Schottky ~0.3V. Applications: rectification (AC→DC), protection, signal demodulation. Zener diode conducts in reverse at its breakdown voltage — used as a voltage reference/regulator.

entries.title: LED
entries.content: LED converts current to light. Forward voltage Vf: red ~1.8-2.0V, green/yellow ~2.0-2.2V, blue/white ~3.0-3.4V. Typical current 20 mA. Always use a series resistor: R = (Vs − Vf)/I. Example: 5V supply, red LED → (5−2)/0.02 = 150Ω → use 150-220Ω.

entries.title: Transistor
entries.content: A transistor is a current/voltage controlled switch and amplifier. BJT (NPN/PNP): current-driven, Ic = β×Ib (β ~100). MOSFET: voltage-driven, very high input impedance, ideal for switching/power electronics. Package examples: BC547 (small signal NPN), IRFZ44N (power N-MOSFET). Legs: Base/Collector/Emitter (BJT), Gate/Drain/Source (MOSFET).

entries.title: Logic Gates
entries.content: Logic gates process binary signals. AND (1 only if both 1), OR (1 if any 1), NOT (invert), NAND = AND+NOT (universal gate), NOR (universal), XOR (1 if inputs differ). CMOS ICs: 4000 series, 74HC00 (NAND), 74HC08 (AND). All digital computers are built from these.

entries.title: Microcontroller vs Microprocessor
entries.content: Microcontroller (MCU): CPU + RAM + Flash + I/O on one chip — runs one program, e.g., 8051, ATmega328 (Arduino Uno), ESP32, STM32. Microprocessor (MPU): CPU only, needs external RAM/storage/IO — runs full OS, e.g., Intel/AMD, ARM Cortex-A (Raspberry Pi). MCUs suit real-time control; MPUs suit general computing.
